0.long_answer: Jacobsen syndrome, also known as the terminal 11q deletion syndrome, is a rare congenital disorder that arises from a deletion on the q arm of chromosome 11. This deletion leads to the loss of several genes, resulting in a spectrum of physical and developmental issues. Individuals with Jacobsen syndrome typically display dysmorphic facial features, intellectual disabilities, delayed development, and other physical problems, such as heart defects and bleeding disorders, often referred to as Paris-Trousseau syndrome. The severity of these symptoms can vary based on the extent of the genetic loss, which may range from 5 to 16 million base pairs.
